missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Дождь' is a masculine noun in the nominative as the subject of 'идёт'. 'Сильный' agrees in the masculine, and 'на улице' is prepositional of location.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Дождь' is the inanimate accusative direct object of 'обещают', matching the nominative form. 'Завтра' adds the time.
Strategic focus: Genitive after 'нет'. 'Дождя' is the genitive required by 'нет' to express absence. The soft -ь noun takes the -я genitive ending.
Strategic focus: Genitive after 'от'. 'От дождя' uses the genitive 'дождя' after 'от' to show the cause. A natural way to explain why the ground is wet.
Strategic focus: Dative with 'рад'. 'Дождю' is the dative governed by the short adjective 'рады'. 'Растения' is the nominative plural subject.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after 'под'. 'Под дождём' uses the instrumental 'дождём' after 'под' to mean walking in the rain. A vivid, common weather phrase.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after 'под'. 'Под дождём' again takes the instrumental 'дождём' to describe the conditions. The stress shifts to the ending in this form.
Strategic focus: Prepositional after 'при'. 'При дожде' uses the prepositional 'дожде' to mean under rainy conditions. 'Скользкой' is the instrumental predicate.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Дожди' is the nominative plural of 'дождь', the subject of 'идут'. 'Осенью' is the instrumental used adverbially for season.
Strategic focus: Prepositional plural. 'О дождях' uses the prepositional plural 'дождях' after 'о' to name the topic. 'Весенних' agrees in the plural prepositional.
